Gre-Nal Showdown: Inter and Grêmio ⁣Battle​ It Out in High-Stakes Clash The first Gre-Nal of ‌the season, coached by Gustavo Quinteros for Grêmio and‍ Roger Machado for Inter, took​ place in the arena.​ While the ⁣home team had the ‌upper hand,the⁢ match ended in ​a 1-1 draw,putting Grêmio’s top spot in⁤ Group A ‌at risk and ‍potentially jeopardizing Inter’s remarkable post-season campaign.
A Classic with Twists and Turns No surprises marked the lineups, and the‍ game unfolded as expected—rugged,⁤ with complaints about the referee, nervousness, an expulsion, and few clear goal opportunities in the first half. ‍Inter’s left side was notably dangerous, with ⁢Wesley and Bernabei ‍imposing themselves.‌ Grêmio’s defensive⁢ left side, however, proved vulnerable, especially with the young defender Vieri under pressure.
At 28 minutes,a controversial decision ‍by referee Rafael Klein ⁢changed the ⁣game’s tone. After hesitating and not issuing a card to Fernando,⁢ Klein gave a ​yellow‍ to ⁤João Pedro, ‍leading to an uproar. Roger Machado’s assistant,Roberto Ribas,was shown a⁣ red card,increasing the‌ technical staff’s indignation. Disgusted, Roger left the field amidst boos.
A Defensive ​Battle Grêmio struggled to create meaningful opportunities,relying heavily on direct balls‌ with little effect. The⁤ midfield failed to generate plays, and the attack went unserved.⁣ Despite Pavón’s efforts, his shot went over the goal, keeping the⁤ score at zero.
Second Half Intensity The‍ second half began with Inter’s aggressive play. Grando saved a shot by ⁢Borré, ⁤and Victor Gabriel missed the rebound. Soon after, Thiago Maia also completed a pass. Grêmio’s response came from a set piece, where Wanderson’s subtle ⁣elbow on the ball led ​to a penalty. Braitewhite converted,putting Grêmio⁣ ahead. Inter quickly equalized with a header‍ from Fernando.
Roger‍ Machado brought on ‍Bruno Henrique and Vitinho,while Gustavo Quinteros substituted Edenilson and Monsalve. Grêmio’s steering wheel moved to the left side of ‍the attack,reinforcing their offensive strategy. In the 44th minute, Valencia’s cross narrowly missed Vitinho’s ​header.
